text: The NHIS Patient Rights agent combines semantic retrieval over policy-style text with structured checks for medicines and facilities. Narrative policy documents are chunked by section for embedding; accredited facilities and the medicines formulary are treated as structured lists for exact or fuzzy lookup. The agent decides which path fits the user question.

Knowledge for Ghana NHIS entitlement guidance is organized by category: coverage (what services and benefits apply), medicines (official formulary entries and prescriber levels), facilities (accreditation and facility type by region), enrollment (membership, registration, renewal), and disputes (denials, incorrect charges, and escalation). Each retrieved chunk should be tagged with one of these domains for filtering when needed.

For RAG ingestion: narrative policy text (benefit package, membership guidelines, dispute procedures) belongs in a vector store with section-aware chunking, not arbitrary character splits. Structured lists such as accredited facilities and the medicines formulary are best stored as CSV or SQL for precise lookup; they can still be converted to natural-language records for hybrid search. Always cite source files and rows when answering.

Evaluation scenarios for the agent include: coverage queries (e.g. whether dialysis or surgery types are covered), drug entitlement (whether a medication should be charged), facility accreditation (whether a hospital is NHIS-accredited), membership and renewal (expired card, re-registration), and rights disputes (being turned away or charged for covered care). Aim for diverse test cases across these intents.

When policy text is silent, sources conflict, or the situation is urgent or high-stakes, the agent should escalate: suggest contacting NHIA or the relevant regional office, collecting receipts and NHIS ID, and using official channels. Do not present model guesses as legal determinations of entitlement.

Authoritative sources to grow the knowledge base include: the NHIS benefit package document, the official NHIS medicines list, accredited facilities by region, membership registration and renewal guidelines, and common denial or dispute resolution procedures. New material should be tagged by category and effective date when known. Place new datasets in the database/ folder and run build_from_database.py.

NHIS KNOWLEDGE BASE

Benefits Package — Chunked & Tagged

Source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits   |   Verified: April 2026

Component: NHIS Patient Rights & Entitlement Agent

What this document is

This is the Knowledge Base source document for the NHIS Patient Rights Agent. It takes the raw content from the NHIA benefits page and breaks it into individual 'chunks' — each one labelled with a metadata tag (ID, category, subcategory, source, date). These chunks are what get loaded into the vector database for the agent to search from when a patient asks a question.

Each coloured box below is one chunk. The green bar at the top of every chunk contains the metadata tag — copy this exactly when loading into your database.

Colour key:

Green = Coverage (covered services)

Red = Exclusions (NOT covered)

Amber = Notes / caveats

Blue = Contact / escalation

SECTION 1 — OUTPATIENT SERVICES

ID: coverage_opd_001   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: outpatient:general]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

General outpatient conditions covered

NHIS covers consultations (including specialist reviews) and treatment for the following conditions at outpatient facilities:

Malaria

Acute respiratory tract infection

Diarrhoeal disease

Skin diseases and ulcers

Hypertension

Acute eye infections

Rheumatism

Anaemia

Intestinal worm disorders

Acute ear infections

Typhoid fever

Dental caries

Diabetes mellitus

Sexually transmitted infections (STIs)

Asthma

Other general and specialist conditions approved by the Minister of Health

ID: coverage_opd_002   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: outpatient:investigations]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Outpatient investigations and diagnostics

The following diagnostic services are covered under NHIS for outpatient and specialist visits at accredited facilities. No co-payment is required for these.

Laboratory investigations (blood tests, urine tests, etc.)

X-rays

Ultrasound scans (for general and specialist outpatient care)

ID: coverage_opd_003   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: outpatient:surgical]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Outpatient and day surgical operations

The following surgical procedures can be performed on an outpatient or day-case basis and are fully covered under NHIS:

Hernia repairs

Incision and drainage of abscesses

Excision of lumps

Haemorrhoidectomy (surgical removal of haemorrhoids)

ID: coverage_opd_004   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: outpatient:hiv]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

HIV/AIDS — symptomatic outpatient treatment

NHIS covers HIV/AIDS symptomatic treatment for opportunistic infections at the outpatient level. This means treatment for the infections that arise because of HIV is covered. IMPORTANT: HIV antiretroviral (ARV) medicines themselves are NOT on the NHIS medicines list and are not covered — they are provided through the separate National AIDS Programme. Do not confuse symptomatic treatment of opportunistic infections with ARV coverage.

ID: coverage_opd_005   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: outpatient:physiotherapy]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Outpatient physiotherapy

Outpatient physiotherapy is covered under NHIS at accredited facilities that offer this service. This includes standard physiotherapy sessions prescribed following injury, surgery, or a medical condition. Note: rehabilitation services other than physiotherapy are excluded (see exclusions section).

ID: coverage_opd_006   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: outpatient:medicines]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Outpatient medicines

Medicines prescribed at outpatient visits are covered if and only if they appear on the official NHIS Medicines List. Two types of medicines are covered:

Prescription medicines on the NHIS Medicines List (551 medicines as of March 2025)

Traditional medicines approved by the Food and Drugs Board and prescribed by an accredited medical or traditional medicine practitioner

SECTION 2 — INPATIENT SERVICES

ID: coverage_inp_001   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: inpatient:general]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

General inpatient care

When admitted to hospital, the following are covered in full under NHIS at any accredited facility:

General and specialist inpatient care

Laboratory investigations, X-rays, and ultrasound scans

Accommodation in the general ward

Feeding (where available at the facility)

Inpatient physiotherapy

Processing for blood and blood products

ID: coverage_inp_002   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: inpatient:surgical]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Inpatient surgical operations

Most surgical operations performed on an inpatient basis are covered under NHIS. This includes major operations such as appendicectomy (removal of the appendix). The general principle is that surgery required to treat a covered condition is itself covered.

ID: coverage_inp_003   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: inpatient:cancer]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Cancer — what is and is not covered for inpatients

NHIS has a specific and limited cancer coverage policy that patients must understand clearly:

COVERED: Cervical cancer treatment (fully covered)

COVERED: Breast cancer treatment (fully covered)

COVERED: Diagnosis and treatment of complications arising from other cancers — for example, anaemia caused by cancer, or bowel obstruction from a tumour

NOT COVERED: Treatment of cancers other than cervical and breast cancer (see exclusions)

ID: coverage_inp_004   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: inpatient:medicines]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Inpatient medicines

Medicines administered during an inpatient stay are covered if they are on the NHIS Medicines List or are traditional medicines approved by the Food and Drugs Board and prescribed by an accredited practitioner. Any medicine not on the NHIS list is not covered and should not be charged to your NHIS card.

SECTION 3 — MATERNITY CARE

ID: coverage_mat_001   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: maternity:full]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Full maternity care — all stages covered at no cost

NHIS provides complete maternity care coverage at no cost to the patient. All of the following are covered in full at any NHIA-accredited facility. No co-payment is required at any stage:

Antenatal care (all antenatal visits throughout the pregnancy)

Normal delivery

Assisted delivery

Caesarean section (C-section) — fully covered, no additional charge

Post-natal care

ID: coverage_mat_002   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: maternity:dispute]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Maternity — common dispute scenario

If a facility asks you to pay for a delivery or caesarean section, this is incorrect. NHIS covers all maternity care including C-sections with no co-payment. If this happens: (1) Politely show your valid NHIS card and ask to speak with the administrator, (2) if unresolved, call the NHIA helpline on 0544446447. Do not leave the facility without escalating — you are entitled to this care at no cost.

SECTION 4 — ORAL HEALTH

ID: coverage_oral_001   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: oral_health]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Oral health services covered

The following dental services are covered under NHIS:

Pain relief — incision and drainage, tooth extraction, temporary pain relief

Dental restoration — simple amalgam fillings and temporary dressing

SECTION 5 — EYE CARE SERVICES

ID: coverage_eye_001   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: eye_care]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Eye care services covered

The following eye care services are covered under NHIS at accredited facilities:

Refraction (eye test to determine prescription for glasses)

Visual fields assessment

Eye scan

Keratometry (measuring the curvature of the cornea's anterior surface)

Cataract removal surgery

Eyelid surgery

SECTION 6 — EMERGENCY SERVICES

ID: coverage_emg_001   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: emergency]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

All emergencies are covered

NHIS covers all emergency health situations that demand urgent intervention. This is a broad, comprehensive category — you cannot be refused emergency care or asked to pay upfront because of your NHIS status. Emergency types covered include:

Medical emergencies

Surgical emergencies — including brain surgery or heart surgery due to accidents

Paediatric (children's) emergencies

Obstetric and gynaecological emergencies — including emergency caesarean sections

Road traffic accidents (RTAs)

Industrial and workplace accidents

ID: coverage_emg_002   [category: coverage]  [subcategory: emergency:brain_heart]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

Important: brain and heart surgery — accidents vs. non-accidents

There is a critical distinction here that the agent must handle correctly. Brain surgery and heart surgery have two different coverage rules depending on cause: (1) Brain or heart surgery RESULTING FROM AN ACCIDENT is covered under the emergency category. (2) Brain or heart surgery NOT resulting from an accident (i.e. elective or disease-based) is listed under exclusions and is NOT covered. Always ask whether the cause is accident-related when advising on this.

SECTION 7 — EXCLUSIONS (NOT COVERED)

The following services and items are explicitly excluded from NHIS coverage. Telling a patient any of these are covered would be a critical error. Each exclusion is a separate chunk so the agent can retrieve them independently.

ID: exclusion_001   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: rehabilitation]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Rehabilitation (other than physiotherapy)

Rehabilitation services are excluded from NHIS, with the single exception of physiotherapy. This means services such as occupational therapy, speech therapy, and other rehabilitation programs are not covered.

ID: exclusion_002   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: appliances]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Appliances and prostheses

Medical appliances and prosthetic devices are not covered. This includes: optical aids (glasses, contact lenses), hearing aids, orthopaedic aids (braces, splints, artificial limbs), and dentures.

ID: exclusion_003   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: cosmetic_surgery]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Cosmetic and aesthetic surgery (with one exception)

Cosmetic surgeries and aesthetic treatments are not covered. EXCEPTION: Reconstructive surgery such as that performed on burns patients IS covered under NHIS. If a patient asks about cosmetic surgery, the answer is no — but if they ask about burns reconstruction or medical reconstructive surgery, the answer may be yes.

ID: exclusion_004   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: hiv_arvs]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: HIV antiretroviral (ARV) medicines

HIV antiretroviral medicines are explicitly excluded from the NHIS Medicines List and are not covered by NHIS. They are provided through the separate National AIDS Programme. Important distinction: treatment of HIV-related opportunistic infections (e.g. treating TB in an HIV patient) IS covered at the outpatient level — but the ARV drugs themselves are not.

ID: exclusion_005   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: assisted_reproduction]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Assisted reproduction

Assisted reproduction procedures are not covered. This includes artificial insemination (IVF and other fertility treatments) and gynaecological hormone replacement therapy.

ID: exclusion_006   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: echocardiography]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Echocardiography

Echocardiography (a painless test that uses sound waves to create moving pictures of the heart, giving information about its size, shape, and function) is not covered under NHIS.

ID: exclusion_007   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: photography]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Clinical photography

Clinical photography — photographs taken in clinics or hospitals to give visual records of a patient's condition and operations for tracking treatment progress in medical files — is not covered under NHIS.

ID: exclusion_008   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: angiography]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Angiography

Angiography — a procedure where a dye is injected into the blood vessels and an X-ray or photograph of the vessels is taken to assess blockages or abnormalities — is not covered under NHIS.

ID: exclusion_009   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: orthoptics]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Orthoptics

Orthoptics — the diagnosis and treatment of defective eye movements and coordination (e.g. for squint/strabismus correction therapy) — is not covered. Note: general eye care such as cataract removal and eyelid surgery IS covered.

ID: exclusion_010   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: dialysis]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Dialysis for chronic kidney failure

Dialysis for chronic kidney failure is explicitly excluded from NHIS coverage. This is an important and commonly asked question — patients with chronic renal failure cannot use NHIS to pay for dialysis sessions. Note: as of 2024, there were government announcements about limited dialysis additions — always verify the current policy before advising, as this may have been updated.

ID: exclusion_011   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: brain_heart_noaccident]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Heart and brain surgery (non-accident)

Heart and brain surgery that does not result from an accident is not covered. Only brain surgery or heart surgery that directly results from a road traffic accident, workplace accident, or other traumatic accident is covered under the emergency category.

ID: exclusion_012   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: cancer_general]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Cancer treatment (except cervical and breast)

Cancer treatment is only covered for cervical cancer and breast cancer. Treatment for all other types of cancer — including prostate cancer, lung cancer, colon cancer, liver cancer, lymphoma, leukaemia, and all others — is not covered. Diagnosis and treatment of complications arising from any cancer (e.g. anaemia, obstruction) IS covered.

ID: exclusion_013   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: organ_transplant]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Organ transplantation

Organ transplantation procedures of any kind are not covered under NHIS. This includes kidney transplants, liver transplants, heart transplants, and all other organ or tissue transplant procedures.

ID: exclusion_014   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: non_nhis_medicines]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Medicines not on the NHIS Medicines List

Any medicine that does not appear on the official NHIS Medicines List is not covered and cannot be charged to your NHIS card. The 2025 list contains 551 medicines described by their generic (INN) names. If a pharmacy tries to charge you for a medicine, check whether its generic name is on the list. Branded versions of listed medicines should still be dispensed — the patient should not pay if the generic equivalent is on the list.

ID: exclusion_015   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: treatment_abroad]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Diagnosis and treatment abroad

Any medical diagnosis or treatment sought outside Ghana is not covered by NHIS. NHIS only covers services delivered within Ghana at NHIA-accredited facilities.

ID: exclusion_016   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: medicals]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Medical examinations for non-clinical purposes

Medical examinations carried out for purposes other than treatment are not covered. This includes: employment medicals, school admission medicals, visa application medicals, and driving licence medicals.

ID: exclusion_017   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: vip_ward]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: VIP ward accommodation

VIP ward accommodation is not covered under NHIS. NHIS covers general ward accommodation only. If a patient chooses to be admitted to a VIP or private room, the additional cost is their personal expense.

ID: exclusion_018   [category: exclusions]  [subcategory: mortuary]  [source: nhis.gov.gh/benefits]  [date: 2026-04]

NOT covered: Mortuary services

Mortuary services are not covered under NHIS. Families of deceased patients are responsible for mortuary fees.

Section 3 — Dispute Scenarios (Step-by-Step)

Scenario A — Charged for a Covered Service

If an accredited NHIS facility charges you for a service that should be covered under your NHIS benefits:

1

Show your valid NHIS card and ask to speak with the facility administrator. State clearly that you are an active NHIS member and that the service should be covered.

2

If the facility administrator does not resolve the issue, call the NHIA patient helpline: 0544446447 or the main office: 0302 238136. Have the facility name and date of visit ready.

3

Follow up in writing by sending an email to info@nhia.gov.gh. Include: facility name, date of service, service you were charged for, and amount paid. Keep any receipt.

4

If unresolved after the email, escalate to the NHIA regional office for your area and request a formal complaint reference number.

CHUNK 2 — Scenario A: Charged for a Covered Service

Step 1: Show valid NHIS card and ask to speak with the facility administrator.

Step 2: If unresolved at facility level, call 0544446447 or 0302 238136.

Step 3: Follow up by email to info@nhia.gov.gh with: facility name, date, and what you were charged for.

Step 4: If still unresolved, escalate to the NHIA regional office and request a formal complaint reference number.

Key rule: NHIS members must NOT be subjected to out-of-pocket payments at accredited facilities.

Always keep receipts of any charges as evidence for your complaint.

[category: disputes]  [tags: covered service, charged, out-of-pocket, escalation, facility administrator]

Scenario B — Facility Denying NHIS Service

If an accredited NHIS facility refuses to provide a covered service or refuses to accept your NHIS card:

1

Confirm the facility is NHIA-accredited (ask for their accreditation certificate or check the NHIA website). If accredited, they are legally obligated to accept NHIS members.

2

Show your valid NHIS card and state: 'This facility is NHIA-accredited. I am an active NHIS member requesting a covered service.'

3

If still denied, call the NHIA patient helpline immediately: 0544446447. You can call from the facility itself — NHIA staff may speak to the facility on your behalf.

4

Email info@nhia.gov.gh with: facility name, accreditation number (if visible), date, service denied, and name of staff member who denied you.

CHUNK 3 — Scenario B: Facility Denying NHIS Service

Policy directive: NHIS members must NOT be subjected to out-of-pocket payments at accredited facilities.

Step 1: Confirm the facility is NHIA-accredited. If yes, they are obligated to serve NHIS members.

Step 2: Show NHIS card and assert your right to the covered service.

Step 3: Call 0544446447 from the facility if service is still denied — NHIA may intervene directly.

Step 4: Email info@nhia.gov.gh with facility name, accreditation number, date, service denied, and staff name.

Note: Denial of service at an accredited facility is a reportable policy violation.

[category: disputes]  [tags: service denial, accredited facility, patient rights, policy directive]

Scenario C — Pharmacy Charging for a Listed Medicine

If a pharmacy refuses to dispense an NHIS-listed medicine without charge, or claims they do not have the NHIS version:

1

Check that your prescription uses the generic name from the NHIS medicines list (e.g., 'Amoxicillin' not a brand name). Personal abbreviations and brand-only names are not accepted on NHIS claims forms.

2

If the pharmacy says they do not have the NHIS version, ask: 'Is there a generic equivalent on the NHIS medicines list?' The generic must be dispensed if available.

3

Do not pay for a branded version without first confirming there is no generic on the NHIS list. You can verify by calling 0544446447 or checking the official NHIA medicines list.

4

If the pharmacy still refuses or charges you for a listed medicine, report the pharmacy name, location, and prescription details to info@nhia.gov.gh or call 0302 238136.

CHUNK 4 — Scenario C: Pharmacy Charging for a Listed Medicine

Rule: Medicines must be prescribed using the generic names on the NHIS medicines list.

Personal abbreviations and brand-only names are NOT accepted on NHIS claims forms.

If a pharmacy says they lack the NHIS version, ask for a generic equivalent from the list before paying for a branded version.

You can verify whether a medicine is on the NHIS list by calling: 0544446447.

To report a pharmacy charging for a listed medicine: email info@nhia.gov.gh or call 0302 238136.

Note: The NHIA medicines formulary (2025 edition) lists all covered medicines by generic name.

Section 4 — Frequently Asked Questions (Disputes)

CHUNK 5 — FAQ: Can a facility charge a NHIS member a top-up fee?

Generally, accredited facilities may not charge NHIS members for covered services.

Some facilities charge 'consultation fees' or 'registration fees' for non-covered items. These are not always improper, but should be clearly itemised.

If you are charged for something you believe is covered by NHIS, follow the Scenario A escalation path above.

If uncertain whether a service is covered, call 0544446447 to verify before the appointment.

[category: disputes]  [tags: top-up fee, extra charges, covered services, FAQ]

CHUNK 6 — FAQ: What if my NHIS card is expired at the point of service?

If your NHIS membership card has expired, the facility may decline to provide NHIS-covered services.

You should renew your membership before attending a facility. Renewal can be done at any NHIA district office.

If you renewed but your card still shows an old date, bring your renewal receipt as proof of active membership.

Call 0544446447 for guidance if a renewed member is being denied service due to a card date issue.

[category: disputes]  [tags: expired card, renewal, membership, denied service, FAQ]

CHUNK 7 — FAQ: What is the waiting period for new or defaulting members?

New members: There is a three-month waiting period from the date of registration before benefits begin.

Defaulters (members who allowed their membership to lapse and are re-registering): A one-month waiting period applies before benefits resume.

During the waiting period, members cannot claim NHIS benefits for any service.

Pregnant women and indigents are exempt from waiting periods.

Source: NHIA policy directive, confirmed by GBC Ghana (2025).

Section 2 — NHIS Medicines List

CHUNK 6 — Key Facts: NHIS Medicines List (2025)

The 2025 NHIS Medicines List contains 551 approved medicines.

Medicines are listed by generic (International Non-Proprietary) names — NOT brand names.

The list is reviewed and updated annually in consultation with healthcare providers.

Only credentialed providers can prescribe medicines under NHIS.

Medicines must be prescribed using the exact names on the approved list.

If a pharmacy says they only have the branded version, ask for a generic equivalent first.

Personal abbreviations and brand-only names are NOT accepted on NHIS claims forms.

To verify if a medicine is on the list, call: 0544446447.

3.3 Maternity Care (100% Free)

CHUNK 13 — Maternity Care (Fully Covered)

ALL maternity care is 100% free for registered NHIS members:

— Ante-natal care (all visits and all tests)

— Normal delivery

— Caesarean section deliveries

— Post-natal care (up to 6 weeks after delivery)

— Neonatal care

Pregnant women are EXEMPT from NHIS premiums entirely.

Pregnant women are also exempt from the 3-month waiting period.

A facility that charges a registered member for maternity care is in violation of NHIS policy.

Section 4 — Services NOT Covered (Exclusions)

CHUNK 18 — Medical Procedures Not Covered

The following medical procedures are excluded from the NHIS benefits package:

— Cosmetic surgery (unless medically necessary)

— Organ transplants

— Dialysis for chronic renal failure (EXCEPT at the 20 designated free dialysis centres)

— Most cancer treatments (EXCEPT breast and cervical cancer)

— Echocardiography

— Angiography

— Assisted reproduction services (IVF, surrogacy)

— Experimental or investigational treatments

— Overseas diagnosis and treatment

— VIP or private ward accommodation (only general ward covered)

Section 5 — Exempted Categories (No Premium Required)

CHUNK 20 — Complete List of Exempted Categories

The following categories pay NO premium. They may only pay a small registration/renewal processing fee:

1. Children — All persons below 18 years. Free if at least one parent/guardian is a valid NHIS member.

2. Pregnant Women — Free coverage for ante-natal, delivery, and post-natal care (up to 6 weeks).

3. Elderly (70+) — Persons above 70 years of age. May pay a small processing fee but no premium.

4. SSNIT Contributors — 2.5% deduction from SSNIT contributions serves as their premium.

5. SSNIT Pensioners — All pensioners of SSNIT.

6. Indigents — Persons classified as indigent by the Minister for Social Welfare.

7. Persons with Disabilities — Categories determined by the Minister for Social Welfare.

8. Mental Health Patients — Persons with diagnosed mental disorders.

9. LEAP Beneficiaries — Beneficiaries of the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty program.

Approximately 65% of active NHIS members fall under exempted categories.

▸  SECTION 1 — How to Register as a New Subscriber

ID: enroll_001   |   category: enrollment   |   subcategory: registration-overview   |   source: nhis.gov.gh/membership   |   date: 2025-04

There are two ways to enrol as a new member with the NHIS. The first is manual enrolment by visiting a District NHIS office in person. The second is digital enrolment using the MyNHIS App, available on the Google Play Store and the iOS App Store. Both methods result in full NHIS membership and require annual renewal.

▸  SECTION 2 — Manual Enrolment (District Office)

ID: enroll_002   |   category: enrollment   |   subcategory: manual-registration   |   source: nhis.gov.gh/membership   |   date: 2025-04

To enrol manually, visit your nearest NHIS District office. An enrolment officer will interview you to determine which membership category you fall into: (a) a fee-paying member who contributes an annual premium, or (b) a member of the exempt group who does not pay any fee. Bring your Ghana Card and any relevant exemption documents.

ID: enroll_003   |   category: enrollment   |   subcategory: registration-documents   |   source: nhis.gov.gh/membership   |   date: 2025-04

At enrolment, you must provide: (a) Full name, (b) Date of birth, (c) Age, (d) Marital status, (e) Mobile phone number(s), (f) Residential address, and (g) Ghana Card details. After recording your details and receiving payment, the enrolment officer will take your photograph and biometric information.

▸  SECTION 3 — Exempt Groups (No Premium Required)

ID: enroll_004   |   category: enrollment   |   subcategory: exemptions-overview   |   source: nhis.gov.gh/membership   |   date: 2025-04

The following people are in the exempt category and do not pay any premium or processing fee: (I) Pregnant women, (II) Persons above 70 years of age, (III) Indigents (persons certified as unable to pay), (IV) Categories of differently-abled persons as determined by the Minister responsible for Social Welfare, and (V) Persons with mental disorders.

ID: enroll_005   |   category: enrollment   |   subcategory: exemption-pregnant-women   |   source: nhis.gov.gh/membership   |   date: 2025-04

A pregnant woman registering for NHIS exemption must present proof of pregnancy. Accepted documents include: a current antenatal card, a signed note from a doctor or midwife, a pregnancy test result endorsed by a doctor or midwife, or an ultrasound scan report interpreted by qualified medical personnel. Note: pregnant women and indigents must enrol in person at a District office — they cannot use the digital platform.

ID: enroll_006   |   category: enrollment   |   subcategory: exemption-ssnit   |   source: nhis.gov.gh/membership   |   date: 2025-04

A SSNIT contributor must provide proof of active SSNIT membership at enrolment — they are then enrolled without paying any premium. SSNIT deducts contributions automatically from formal sector workers' salaries (2.5% of basic salary). A SSNIT pensioner under age 70 must provide their SSNIT number for enrolment without paying any premium.

▸  SECTION 4 — Digital Enrolment (MyNHIS App)

ID: enroll_007   |   category: enrollment   |   subcategory: digital-registration   |   source: nhis.gov.gh/membership   |   date: 2025-04

To enrol digitally, download and install the MyNHIS app from the Google Play Store (Android) or the iOS App Store (iPhone) and follow the on-screen steps. Note: pregnant women and indigents must register at a District office in person — they cannot use the digital platform.

▸  SECTION 5 — Membership Renewal

ID: renew_001   |   category: enrollment   |   subcategory: renewal-overview   |   source: nhis.gov.gh/membership   |   date: 2025-04

NHIS membership is valid for twelve (12) months. Members must renew their membership every year. Membership can be renewed at any NHIS District office, via the USSD code *929#, or through the MyNHIS App. Members are advised to renew within three months of their membership expiry date to avoid defaulter status.

ID: renew_002   |   category: enrollment   |   subcategory: renewal-defaulter-rules   |   source: nhis.gov.gh/membership   |   date: 2025-04

Members who fail to renew within three months after expiry are classified as defaulters. Defaulters must serve a one-month waiting period before accessing healthcare again under NHIS. Exceptions: pregnant women, children under five (5) years old, and persons above seventy (70) years old can access care immediately even after defaulting.

ID: renew_003   |   category: enrollment   |   subcategory: membership-card-amendments   |   source: nhis.gov.gh/membership   |   date: 2025-04

Membership cards that are damaged, defaced, or lost can be replaced at a cost — contact your nearest District NHIS office. Members who need to amend personal details (e.g. name change due to marriage) must provide legal evidence: marriage certificate, birth certificate, affidavit, or gazette notice.

Section 1 — Overview & Timeline

CHUNK 1 — NHIS Legal Framework Overview

The NHIS of Ghana is governed by a comprehensive legal framework establishing rights, responsibilities, and operational procedures for universal health coverage.

Key milestones:

2003 — National Health Insurance Act, 2003 (Act 650) enacted — original framework

2004 — NHIS operations commenced

2008 — National Health Insurance (Amendment) Act, 2008 (Act 753)

2012 — National Health Insurance Act, 2012 (Act 852) — CURRENT governing legislation

2012 onwards — Various Legislative Instruments and Guidelines issued

Act 852 repealed both Acts 650 and 753. It was assented to on October 31, 2012.

It is organised into 4 parts covering 113 sections.

[category: policy]  [tags: legal framework, Act 852, timeline, history, legislation]

CHUNK 2 — Hierarchy of Legal Documents

Level 1 — Acts of Parliament (highest authority) — e.g. Act 852

Level 2 — Legislative Instruments (L.I.) — made by Minister/NHIA

Level 3 — Regulations and Guidelines — issued by NHIA Board

Level 4 — Operational Manuals and Procedures — issued by NHIA

Any conflict between levels is resolved in favour of the higher-level document.

Section 111 of Act 852 provides consequential amendments to related Acts to ensure consistency.

2.2 Key Provisions

CHUNK 4 — Mandatory Membership (Section 27)

All residents of Ghana are required to belong to the National Health Insurance Scheme.

Employers must ensure that their employees are registered.

Source: Section 27, National Health Insurance Act, 2012 (Act 852)

[category: policy]  [tags: mandatory membership, registration, employers, Section 27]

CHUNK 5 — Exemptions from Contributions (Section 29)

The following categories are exempt from paying NHIS premiums:

— Children below 18 years

— Pregnant women

— Persons with mental disorders

— Indigents

— Differently-abled persons (as determined by the Minister)

— SSNIT pensioners and contributors

— Persons above 70 years of age

Approximately 65% of active NHIS members fall under exempted categories.

Exempted members may still be required to pay a small processing fee for registration/renewal.

Source: Section 29, National Health Insurance Act, 2012 (Act 852)

[category: policy]  [tags: exemptions, premium, contributions, children, pregnant, SSNIT, elderly, indigent, Section 29]

CHUNK 6 — National Health Insurance Fund (Sections 39–46)

Sources of funding for the NHIS:

— 2.5% National Health Insurance Levy on goods and services

— 2.5% of SSNIT contributions

— Parliamentary allocations

— Investment returns

— Member premiums

— Grants and donations

The levy is collected by the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) under Act 791.

Source: Sections 39–46, Act 852

CHUNK 8 — NHIS Medicines List

Updated annually. Latest edition: March 2025.

Contains 551 approved medicines derived from the Essential Medicines List.

Lists medicines by generic (International Non-Proprietary) names — NOT brand names.

Includes dosage forms and pricing for each entry.

Only credentialed providers can prescribe NHIS medicines.

Patients should ensure their prescription uses the exact generic name from this list.

Personal abbreviations or brand-only names are not accepted on NHIS claims forms.

Tariffs define how much NHIA pays a provider for each service.
